explanation: Twelve is a traditional symbol of completeness and unity, so the number never changes with membership. The Council of Europe adopted the flag in 1955, decades before the EU took it up.

claims.text: The flag of the European Union shows a circle of 12 gold stars.
The EU flag does not have 6, 15 or 27 stars.
The number of stars on the EU flag is fixed at 12, a symbol of completeness and unity, and does not depend on the number of member states.
The Council of Europe adopted the flag in 1955.
The European Communities adopted the same flag in the 1980s.
